title: Anonymous names, Buck Brand sponsor and staff-band status
summary: The group recorded under invented names, and sponsors included Buck Brand work clothes at $3.50 a program. Staff work gave them standing above other bands.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: What name did you record under? I mean, did you use for these transcriptions?

Ah, something they cook up. The something, I don't know what the, I have no idea. They would whip up something and call it something. Three different names. One for morning, one for noon in the morning. Wake up stuff. Wake up, arise, alert song. And the three different names for the three different groups, but I don't know what they
were. And on none of the shows were their vocals?
No. So they could bring in ads and they brought them in to constantly.
Gee. But then you didn't have any, there was no personal appeal because it was a favorite band. I mean you were essentially an unidentified band.

That is true. We used to play also, we had a Buck brand work clothes. And a fellow would say, excuse me, Buck brand work clothes wear like leather. And then we'd play Leather Bridges for the theme song. Oh great. Why? Buck brand work clothes. Or work clothes in Fort Worth.
Is this the only sponsor you remember?

Those two, that XEPN thing, and then the Buck brand buckaroos twice a week. We used to get paid, it seems to me, three and a half per radio program by the station for those Buck brand buckaroos. We'd get seven dollars a week coming in from that. But in the Depression days, it helped out. But you see, being kind of, this gave us the status of a staff band in a way. And this was above the other groups, the Bill Boyd even, and all those others, Roy Newman, Roy A, all this other stuff. And gave us a little standard. And we. Whenever we had to get substitutes, we'd dip into the other bands. But we could always get the other band members. Where we didn't have very many who left at all. They would die or go off to California. Dick Reinhart going off to California.
